newsitem.title: USA: Painewebber ups WTI '97 forecast by $1.00/barrel.
newsitem.headline: Painewebber ups WTI '97 forecast by $1.00/barrel.

text.p: PaineWebber said it is raising its 1997 price forecast for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude to $21.50 a barrel from $20.50, much above the Wall Street consensus.
The brokerage also raised its 1998 forecast to $22.00 a barrel from $21.00. In a report, PaineWebber listed the First Call 1997 consensus forecast as $19.89 and $19.55 for 1998.

"Because demand growth is increasing, we have finally gotten to the bottom in terms of real oil prices," said PaineWebber's international and domestic oils analyst Steve Pfeifer in an industry conference call.
"This could be a different world where we start to move up in terms of expectations from an $18 to $20 world to a $19 to $23, $24 world," Pfeifer said of WTI's longer term price range.

PaineWebber estimates that 1997 worldwide demand will increase to 74.3 million barrels a day (bpd) from 72.2 million in 1996, with growth driven by energy usage in developing countries such as China and Indonesia.
Demand is rising when worldwide supply is relatively tight, said the firm. Data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) shows U.S. crude stocks as of January 10 off 14 million barrels.
Moreover, the Organization for Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) did not raise its 25.03 million bpd production ceiling at its meeting last November in the face of rising demand.

Although the United Nations is allowing limited oil exports from Iraq under the "oil-for-food" deal, PaineWebber said the 500,000 to 700,000 bpd in Iraqi exports should be easily absorbed by the market.
In December, the United Nations eased sanctions against Iraq and allowed Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, in exchange for humanitarian aid.
PaineWebber said given the worldwide supply and demand outlook for oil, it is recommending that equity investors maintain an overweighted portfolio position in the major oil companies.

Its top picks in the group are British Petroleum, USX-Marathon Group, and Mobil Corp, which carry the firm's "buy" recommendation, and Total S.A. and Texaco Inc, both carrying an "attractive" rating by the firm.
